text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Moslem-Croat federation Prime Minister Edhem Bicakcic, meets former U.S. envoy to Bosnia Richard Sklar, says a model for starting domestic production in Bosnia has been generally adopted.
- Bicakcic urges Bill Clinton's special envoy to Bosnia, John Kornblum, to make efforts to boost federation implementation.

- President of International Helsinki Federation for Human Rights, Jo Benkov, has asked from U.S. State Secretary Madeleine Albright U.S. support for establishment of forces to arrest suspected war criminals, Bosnia's branch of the organisation says.

- Bosnian Serb president Biljana Plavsic meets with Kai Eide, United Nations, special envoy to Bosnia to discuss the situation in the area of disputed town of Brcko after the Vienna conference. Plavsic said that Serbs "will take full responsibility and guarantee security in the region".
- Croatian embassy in Bosnia complains about present anti- Croatian campaign in Sarajevo's media and says that a trend of presenting top Croatian officials in a very inappropriate way continues.

- Brussels agreement from March 6, assigning the control over Bosnia's sky to air controllers from Belgrade and Zagreb, is a new proof that an agremeent to split the country is still effective, Omer Kulic, manager of the state air company Air Bosna, says.
- U.N. international police monitors, IPTF, conduct education seminar for Bosnia's federal policemen.
- Italian children from Prato collected 5,000 toys for their Sarajevo friends to be distributed in children health institutions and kindergartens.
- Bosnia's defence ministry and joint command of the federation army have been finally completed according to adopted regulations proposed by the U.S. military programme "Equip and Train".

- Jerry Robbins, senior adviser to OSCE mission in Bosnia says that Provisional Electoral Commission (PEC) will reconsider date of Bosnia's local polls set for mid September 1997 if the Bosnia's federation parliament does not adopt law on divided municipalities, local news agency Onasa says.
- Sarajevo hosts three-day symposium on civil engeneering and equipment organised by Germany where 34 companies are presented.
- Workers of a civil engineering company from Tuzla went on strike on Thursday due to very low salaries.
- Bosnia's Council of Ministers should decide on Thursday to establish 30 telephone lines between Sarajevo and Pale for local authorities' purposes, a source from Carl Bildt's office says.
- Mostar Mayor Ivan Prskalo recieved an Italian delegation and agreed on a 1.1 million German Marks donation for the southern town. -- Sarajevo newsroom, +387-71-663-864.
